system.name: BDLF-Qwen3
system.one_liner: Cross-architecture binary function similarity detection with Qwen3 plus Binary Dynamic Layer Fusion, trained in two stages on the new Cross-Bin dataset.

content.variant_note: three titled frames chained by yellow arrows (collections, Ghidra pipeline, training with two stacked stages) plus a fourth frame that opens the fusion module, tied to Stage 2 by dashed lines
content.argues: A Ghidra-built cross-architecture dataset and a fusion module that weights all previous layers dynamically let a Qwen3 backbone find similar binary functions across CPU architectures.
content.subject: dataset construction from binaries via Ghidra, two training stages, and the internals of the dynamic layer-fusion module

summary: BDLF-Qwen3 detects similar binary functions across CPU architectures by fusing the outputs of all earlier Qwen3 layers with dynamically generated weights. Figure 1 is made of four rounded frames with orange italic titles. Binary Collections, a stack of ARM32, MIPS64, ARM64 and x86-64 cards, feeds the Ghidra Pipeline (disassemble and decompile with Xref and CFG information, Ghidra and whale logos) that yields the Cross-Bin dataset. Yellow arrows lead to the Training Stage with two stacked boxes: Stage-1 partial fine-tuning of Qwen-3 and Stage-2 BDLF training that ends in an InfoNCE similarity matrix. A fourth frame, tied to Stage 2 by dashed lines, opens the fusion module: layer outputs X_0 to X_2 multiplied by weights A_0 to A_2 and summed.
summary_zh: BDLF-Qwen3 通过动态加权融合 Qwen3 各层输出来检测跨架构的相似二进制函数。图由四个圆角框组成：二进制集合、Ghidra 流水线（产出 Cross-Bin 数据集）、两阶段训练，以及用虚线引出的动态层融合模块内部结构。
notes: No paragraph mentions the figure, so roles rest on the caption, the abstract and the drawing. Unexplained in the figure and caption: the whale logo's role (it joins the arrow into Cross-Bin), the labels DA and T, the exact role of Lambda (read as the weight generator from the abstract), and what the framed Byte-Pair Encoding / Instruction Aware boxes belong to. The panel list counts the four rounded frames; the two stage boxes inside Training Stage are described as containers.
